title: Deployment variance synthesis for multi-mode model rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Rollout configs that work for hosted mode often fail or behave suboptimally in Dedicated and Private due to differences in networking, KMS/HSM availability, autoscaler primitives, node pool sizing, and tenancy constraints. Goal: build a synthesis layer and validation pipeline that ingests a canonical rollout manifest and emits environment-specific deployment plans plus automated preflight checks, diff reports, and mitigation suggestions. Scope includes canary/A-B variants, shadow traffic rules, autoscaling knobs, KV cache warmup, and auto-rollback policies. Non-goals: changing runtime scheduling internals or implementing new autoscalers; we will integrate with existing Dedicated/Private primitives via adapters.
success_criteria:
1) A canonical manifest can be compiled to environment-specific plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private with no manual edits for 90% of supported rollout policies.
2) Preflight validator detects environment incompatibilities with actionable fixes and < 1% false-positive rate in test set.
3) Rollouts using compiled plans pass canary checks and auto-rollback triggers in staging and are usable by Platform and Solutions teams.
